title: Exchange-bias quantum tunnelling in a CO2-based Dy4 single-molecule magnet

synthesis.procedure: Under argon using standard Schlenk technique, anhydrous DyCl3 (6 mmol) in a 100 mL Schlenk tube was heated at 120 °C under vacuum (about 10^-3 mbar) for 1.5 h, cooled to room temperature, and treated with 50 mL dry toluene and 5 mL freshly distilled diisopropylamine. After stirring for 1.5 h, dried CO2 was bubbled through the mixture for about 20 min and the tube was sealed under 1 atm CO2. Stirring was continued for 4 days. The cloudy mixture was filtered and the clear filtrate was kept at 5 °C, giving colourless block crystals after 1 day. The main text describes the same reaction as anhydrous dysprosium chloride with a six-fold excess of diisopropylamine and CO2 in dry toluene.

properties.summary: Compound 1 is a Dy4 single-molecule magnet. DC susceptibility shows depopulation of crystal-field levels and antiferromagnetic interactions. AC data give slow relaxation at zero field and a modestly higher barrier under 1.5 kOe. Micro-SQUID loops open below 2 K and show exchange-biased quantum tunnelling arising from coexisting antiferromagnetic (short Dy···Dy) and ferromagnetic (longer Dy···Dy) pathways.

material_class.structural_family: isotropic Gd4 analogue of the homoleptic tetranuclear carbamate cage

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same Schlenk procedure as compound 1, using anhydrous GdCl3 instead of DyCl3. Anhydrous LnCl3 (6 mmol) was heated at 120 °C under vacuum (about 10^-3 mbar) for 1.5 h, cooled, and combined with 50 mL dry toluene and 5 mL diisopropylamine. After 1.5 h, dried CO2 was bubbled for about 20 min, the tube was sealed under 1 atm CO2, and the slurry was stirred for 4 days, filtered, and crystallized at 5 °C.

properties.summary: The Gd4 analogue was used as the isotropic model of the Dy4 cage. Simultaneous fitting of chi_M T and magnetization supports two exchange pathways, one antiferromagnetic and one ferromagnetic, consistent with the two crystallographically distinct metal–metal contacts.
